    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (439 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Sources indicate that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the latest tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    In a recent development, implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders substantial and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    Breaking: Jensen Huang is ‘too significant to fire,’ putting Nvidia’s governance in focus: analysts

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO may have eased concerns over the chipmaker's leadership, but it has also brought renewed scrutiny to the tech giant's corporate governance and its reliance on its founder.
    • Huang's abrupt departure and unexpected reinstatement exposed a deeper vulnerability at the heart of Nvidia, industry experts told CNBC, raising questions about board oversight and succession planning.
    • "What does it mean if you have a firm too massive to fail or a CEO too big to fire?" Angela Mancini, head of advisory for global risk insights at Dow Jones, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Tuesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO may have eased concerns over the chipmaker's leadership, but it has also brought renewed scrutiny to the tech giant's corporate governance and its reliance on its founder.

    Huang's abrupt departure and unexpected reinstatement exposed a deeper vulnerability at the heart of Nvidia, industry experts told CNBC, raising questions about board oversight and succession planning.

    "What does it mean if you have a firm too massive to fail or a CEO too big to fire?" Angela Mancini, head of advisory for global risk insights at Dow Jones, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Tuesday.

    Mancini pointed to Huang's unusually large number of direct reports as another sign of how heavily Nvidia depends on its founder.

    "What does it mean when someone has 60 direct reports, and you literally are in a situation where you feel like you can't fire them?" she added.

    Industry observers note that nvidia's market cap ballooned from $3 trillion on Friday to almost $4 trillion on Tuesday after Huang was reinstated. "That is what you'd call a founder premium," Yang Wang, a principal analyst at Counterpoint Research, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe.".

    "The reaction has been staggering," Wang remarked. "But is this level of dependence healthy?".

    For Nvidia, Huang's return offers an opportunity to address some of the governance challenges brought to light by his departure.

    Jeff Herbst, managing partner at GFT Ventures and a former Nvidia executive who spent nearly two decades at the company, said he had written to the board late last week calling for Huang's return.

    While initially disappointed by the allegations surrounding Huang, Herbst remarked he came to view the episode as an opportunity for Nvidia to strengthen its governance, succession planning and overall management.

    "While a lot of people saw a crisis here, I saw a potential opportunity," he noted.

    Herbst remarked Nvidia's management and oversight functions needed to evolve alongside its transformation from a relatively small technology company into one of the world's largest corporations.

    "I think the corporate governance, the succession planning, the legal function, the regulatory function, the political function, all has to scale at the same time," he remarked.

    He suggested Nvidia add more experience to its board by bringing in individuals who have run large companies and take a more formal approach to developing potential successors to Huang.

    Tom Hulick, CEO of Strategy Asset Managers, agreed, saying the chip giant's "corporate governance definitely needs to be retooled.".

    It's "unheard of" and "unprecedented" for a president to enforce the reinstatement of a organization's CEO, Hulick mentioned on "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday.

    Industry observers note that "He's a born leader. He's enduring a lot of pain right now. Does he deserve to be back as CEO? It's not for me to speculate. Is he the right person? Probably for now.".

    However, Hulick added that the firm still has "a lot of things to worry about" regarding corporate governance.

    Huang's departure also exposed how closely Nvidia's leadership and long-term strategy are tied to its founder, raising questions about how the company would navigate a future transition.

    It has been revealed that stacy Rasgon, managing director and senior U.S. semiconductor analyst at Bernstein Research, noted the episode had revived attention to a risk investors had long overlooked.

    In a recent development, "We all knew that there was key man risk here. We all chose, and I'm including myself in that. We all kind of chose to just ignore it," Rasgon told CNBC.

    Succession planning, he said, is an issue both Huang and the board will need to address and communicate clearly to investors.

    "I think both Jensen and the board will have to figure out, and I think communicate to investors," he added.

    Herbst also pointed to Huang's personal role in driving Nvidia's technological innovations, including his willingness to invest in artificial intelligence and high-performance computing long before those businesses became profitable.

    Latest markets such as autonomous systems and robotics would require major investment and a leader with Huang's passion and vision, Herbst added.

    Correction: This story has been updated to reflect that Angela Mancini mentioned Nvidia is in a situation where it feels like you can not fire the CEO.

    Amazon to acquire AI startup Decart's chip software, hire founders

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (366 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Amazon is scooping up much of the technology and talent behind artificial intelligence startup Decart, marking the latest reverse acquihire deal by a major tech tech giant.
    • In a Monday blog post, Amazon mentioned it agreed to purchase Decart's "proprietary technology" and hire the startup's three founders, as well as their AI researchers and engineers.
    • The Israeli startup, founded in 2023, is best known for its software that lets developers sync their AI models across different chips, allowing them to switch hardware quickly, known as the Decart Optimization Stack.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Amazon is scooping up much of the technology and talent behind artificial intelligence startup Decart, marking the latest reverse acquihire deal by a major tech tech giant.

    In a Monday blog post, Amazon mentioned it agreed to purchase Decart's "proprietary technology" and hire the startup's three founders, as well as their AI researchers and engineers.

    The Israeli startup, founded in 2023, is best known for its software that lets developers sync their AI models across different chips, allowing them to switch hardware quickly, known as the Decart Optimization Stack.

    "Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip," Peter DeSantis, a senior vice president at Amazon who oversees foundation models, custom silicon and quantum computing development, remarked in a statement. "More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.".

    DeSantis added, "From our earliest work with Decart, we knew they were the kind of technologically fearless team who would help us push it even further.".

    Amazon has moved deeper into building custom AI chips amid insatiable demand for the technology, and as companies seek alternatives to Nvidia, the dominant provider. Amazon has positioned its Trainium and Inferentia chips as lower-cost options for AI developers.

    Last month, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said the company plans to make its Trainium chips externally available for the first time in "late in 2027.".

    Several outlets reported Amazon will pay $7.5 billion for Decart's assets, citing people familiar with the matter. Amazon declined to comment on the terms of the deal.

    Anthropic had considered acquiring Decart and conducted due diligence, but ultimately walked away from a deal, Bloomberg reported.

    Tech companies including Microsoft, Meta and Google have announced a series of deals with buzzy AI startups, which involve licensing their technology or nabbing their top talent and founders. The moves, often referred to as reverse acquihires, stop short of buying the companies outright. Amazon made two similar deals in 2024 when it brought on talent from Adept and Covariant.

    Sources indicate that the arrangements have attracted regulatory scrutiny in some cases. Amazon said Monday the Decart deal is subject to regulatory approval.

    #165057. Breaking: Why France is at risk of recession — and what could keep it out of one

    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Why France is at risk of recession — and what could keep it out of one

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1391 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • France's economy is flashing fresh recession warnings as businesses delay decisions ahead of the 2027 election — but resilient industries, progress on the budget and lower energy costs could help keep growth positive.
    • Business activity declined to a six-month low in November, with manufacturing performing worse than the services sector, according to the S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index published on Monday.
    • The French private sector is at its most pessimistic about the coming year since late 2012, excluding the months at the start of the pandemic, according to the survey, with job losses recorded for a seventh straight month.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    France's economy is flashing fresh recession warnings as businesses delay decisions ahead of the 2027 election — but resilient industries, progress on the budget and lower energy costs could help keep growth positive.

    Business activity declined to a six-month low in November, with manufacturing performing worse than the services sector, according to the S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index published on Monday.

    The French private sector is at its most pessimistic about the coming year since late 2012, excluding the months at the start of the pandemic, according to the survey, with job losses recorded for a seventh straight month.

    Among the biggest challenges cited by companies were economic conditions, uncertainty, competition and cost pressures, while frail domestic demand is weighing on sales.

    France is heading toward a closely watched presidential election in April 2027, with polling suggesting voters may favor candidates offering a break from the policies associated with incumbent President Emmanuel Macron.

    Politico polling this year has consistently indicated the front-runner is far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who has recently made efforts to appease financial market jitters over France's fiscal sustainability, but has failed to convince many analysts that she can stabilize the country's debt trajectory.

    The latest PMI figures add to a run of economic woes for France this year, including a dramatic rise in government borrowing costs, a surprise outlook downgrade by ratings agency Fitch, and a tumbling stock market which has underperformed its European peers.

    This has compounded a sense of crisis after hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets in October and November to protest underfunding in education, the cost of living and the state of public services and housing.

    The latest PMI survey has meanwhile raised the odds of France entering a technical recession — two consecutive prints of negative GDP growth — in the fourth quarter, according to Joe Hayes, senior principal economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. The next print will follow a 0.1% contraction in the third quarter, though a revised Q3 reading is due on Friday.

    "The eurozone's second-largest economy is struggling with weak domestic demand, in part due to hesitancy from clients to commit to projects ahead of a highly uncertain election period next year," Hayes said.

    "We've subsequently seen a rapid deterioration in business confidence these past few months as other long-standing challenges, such as concerns about France's fiscal position, resurface as the election draws closer.".

    Recent findings suggest that "It's also notable that output price inflation has slowed sharply in November. This suggests that tech giant pricing power has diminished and further highlights the fragility of the French economy," Hayes added.

    Sharon Bell, senior European equity strategist at Goldman Sachs, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday that most people had expected a bounce-back in France's PMI figures in Monday's release "on the basis of getting through the worst period of protests.".

    France's worst rioting in years in October not only racked up millions of dollars in insured losses but damaged the country's standing among some international investors, contributing to a sense of instability and an inability to pass reforms.

    Bell stated the gloomy PMI figures demonstrated the weakness of French growth and its additional vulnerability alongside its election risk premium and large deficit.

    A crucial factor for the French economy, according to Bell, will be whether a recent spike in European energy prices will begin to ease.

    Sovereign risk has already started to become less of a distraction from solid European corporate fundamentals as energy pressures have started to let up over the last month, and will continue to do so if that continues, she told CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that "If energy prices do stay high, then obviously that means higher inflation, higher rates, and more of a problem for the more vulnerable sovereigns. And France would definitely be in that group, probably the most vital member of that group at the moment," she said.

    Higher French government bond yields — stoked by a mix of its failure to pass a budget that will reduce the deficit, political paralysis and weak economic growth — have piled pressure on businesses as high rates spill over into corporate borrowing costs, making it more expensive to refinance debt or fund latest projects.

    French homebuilder Nexity remarked in an October trading patch that a 10-year government bond yield near 5% had "reduced household borrowing capacity" as it recorded an 18% fall in sales to individual homebuyers in the first nine months.

    Also in October, office landlord Gecina stated it would be "very careful" about new capital spending amid pressure on its future financing costs, while bank Societe Generale said that the widening gap in French borrowing costs with Germany "could adversely affect the funding conditions of the Group and its clients.".

    Uncertainty around the outcome of the election, in which the far-left Jean-Luc Mélenchon is another popular candidate, is also frequently cited by analysts as deterring French business activity and investment.

    Helene Gans, president and co-founder of investment fund Renaissance Capital, said in an opinion piece for Economie Matin earlier in November that companies are postponing decision-making, delaying near-finalized commitments and dragging out negotiations with a "worrying intensity" — attributing the fall in confidence to the run-up to the 2027 election.

    However, Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin told CNBC's Charlotte Reed in an exclusive interview last week that he does not forecast a recession, even if the central bank's current projection for 0.4% growth in the fourth quarter "might be a little bit too high.".

    "We don't see a recession coming, we see positive growth in Q4," Moulin told CNBC.

    According to recent reports, "We have a survey every month of 8,500 companies, and we ask them whether their activity will grow in the next month, and there is a resilience of industry and of services in France, and in particular for industries and sectors that are doing well, like electricity, defense, aeronautics. These sectors are showing resilience and weathering the global shocks that we are seeing," he stated.

    Moulin nonetheless cited a lack of confidence and political uncertainty as key factors holding back economic performance this year.

    Recent findings suggest that "We are seeing ... worries about the situation of public finance, and this triggers high saving rates, worries about the future of pensions, and so all this tends to lower consumption, tends to be, you know, reducing investment," he stated.

    On borrowing costs, Moulin remarked spreads with nations such as Germany were "very high, and too high.".

    "They are too high compared with the situation of the French economy, its trends, but also its fiscal situation, which is not good, which needs to be dealt with, but which has not changed materially from, you know, June to September," he added.

    Industry observers note that "So there is some kind of, I think, overreaction of the markets. But I think it's notable for the government to give signs that they are serious about reducing the deficit.".

    Moulin said that he was confident that the government's current budget proposal, designed to narrow the country's deficit from 5.4% of GDP to 5% of GDP, will be passed, even if it requires an executive decree or another measure if it fails to pass through the divided parliament.

    French finance minister Roland Lescure said on Monday that the government's 2027 economic growth forecast of 1% was at risk of being downgraded, as he also backed the prospect of a budgetary "golden rule" — a reform that would impose stricter controls on public spending and would look to stop governments from running excessive deficits.

    Le Pen proposed a golden rule in a recent speech, a concept that has also been backed by centrist candidate Edouard Philippe.

    Moulin told CNBC last week that such a move would "enshrine the fiscal discipline in our institutions.".

    Recent findings suggest that "Most of the [presidential] candidates have, you know, been quite affirmative in their resolution to reduce the deficit. All of them are making pleas... advocating that they will reduce the deficit down to 3%," he remarked.

    In a recent development, "The consensus over reducing the deficit is broadening, but we don't need only words. We need acts, and the first act, I think, in order to show that the government is serious about fiscal discipline, is to have a budget.".

    #165054. Breaking: Signal joins United Airlines, banks in limiting AI agents over customer risks

    Breaking: Signal joins United Airlines, banks in limiting AI agents over customer risks

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Privacy-focused messaging application Signal is tightening protections against artificial intelligence agents that can access information displayed on users' screens, citing concerns over privacy and security.
    • Signal said AI agents built into mobile operating systems, such as Google's Gemini and Apple's Siri with onscreen awareness, can "scan" information on owners' screens, potentially capturing and storing Signal data outside its control.
    • The company said it will block screenshots in its iOS app and, on Android, enable screen security when it detects an AI assistant attempting to read the screen.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Privacy-focused messaging application Signal is tightening protections against artificial intelligence agents that can access information displayed on users' screens, citing concerns over privacy and security.

    Signal said AI agents built into mobile operating systems, such as Google's Gemini and Apple's Siri with onscreen awareness, can "scan" information on owners' screens, potentially capturing and storing Signal data outside its control.

    The company said it will block screenshots in its iOS app and, on Android, enable screen security when it detects an AI assistant attempting to read the screen.

    "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal — and application developers beyond — lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," Meredith Whittaker, president of the app's nonprofit parent Signal Foundation, said in a Friday blog post.

    Industry observers note that signal last year introduced similar restrictions against Microsoft's Recall AI on Windows 11. Its latest move adds to a broader push by companies including United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab to limit or block AI agents over security and for customer-protection concerns.

    Whittaker noted the new protections do not address every way an agent might gain access to data, including by retrieving content already stored on a user's device.

    Signal also warned that third-party agents such as Meta's Muse could gain access to private app content through permissions granted during setup.

    "Application-level protections will always have gaps, so the data an agent can reach has to be classified, permissioned and recoverable before the agent arrives," said Tianyi Jiang, CEO of data management and protection software company AvePoint.

    In a recent development, avePoint's State of AI 2026 report found that 88.4% of surveyed organizations had experienced at least one AI-agent-related security breach in the previous year. The survey covered 750 IT leaders globally.

    "We continue to call on the major consumer operating system companies – Apple, Google and Microsoft – to provide simple technical tools and accurate documentation that give developers like Signal ways to prevent AI agents from accessing sensitive application data," remarked Whittaker.

    Banks are also restricting third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts.

    JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon mentioned in October that outside agents were too risky for the bank and its clients. Morgan Stanley has blocked third-party agents from its platforms, Reuters reported.

    Meanwhile, Charles Schwab CEO Richard Wurster said the brokerage blocks unauthorized agents to protect clients and the firm.

    Singapore's OCBC Bank has said it will not let third-party agents to interact with the bank to transfer money autonomously and warned that "customers should exercise caution" when using such agents for banking.

    United Airlines said Nov. 11 that it would restrict unauthorized agents from booking or managing tickets, citing risks that they could expose customer information, make unintended purchases or violate aviation rules.

    "To book flights or do your grocery shop, an agent needs your email, accounts and payment details," mentioned Mick Maleishko, an AI advocate at identity verification and compliance platform Sumsub.

    He stated that level of access creates a risk of account hijacking because actions taken by an agent may appear to a retailer or bank to have been authorized by the user.

    Sources indicate that singapore Airlines, by contrast, is an early partner of Meta's Muse. Meta mentioned people can ask the agent to explore travel, ticketing and reservation options through the airline.

    According to recent reports, "People treat agent risk as one-size-fits-all rather than matching the security needed to the actual task," noted Yat Siu, executive chairman and co-founder of Animoca Brands. He said agents could help consumers act on their intentions and help businesses reach customers directly, but the risks vary by task.

    Recent findings suggest that "There's a much higher risk around an agent able to move meaningful sums of money or access sensitive personal data, than one making your restaurant reservations," Siu stated. "The reality is that, just like internet applications to date, agents require tiered safeguards.".

    #165053. Breaking: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 12: Is it time to start taking the Giants seriously?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 25m • 📚 Deep Dive (5095 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 12: Is it time to start taking the Giants seriously?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks.
    • AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers.
    • Before Week 11, the New York Giants had a perception problem.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks.

    AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers.

    Before Week 11, the New York Giants had a perception problem.

    They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics noted they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East.

    Then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start. They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams. It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being said about the Giants.

    Recent findings suggest that "We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play.".

    Yet, they knew what was being mentioned about them.

    Sources indicate that "They keep saying we can't beat these teams, we can't beat them. I don't know why they're saying that," edge rusher Abdul Carter said, according to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein. "But what are they going to say now?".

    According to recent reports, the Giants' upset win over the Jaguars changes things. It boosts their chances of making the playoffs as a division champion. The way the Giants' defense played, holding the Jaguars without a touchdown for the first three quarters, gives hope of a strong finish to the year after a first half of the season that lacked a quality win. The offense is still not great, ranking 22nd in DVOA. But J.J. McCarthy makes a few plays each game that also provide some optimism, Malik Nabers is one of the NFL's best receivers, Isaiah Likely is having a breakout season and Cam Skattebo generally provides at least a reasonable run game.

    The Giants likely aren't going to challenge the 49ers or whoever wins the NFC North for a Super Bowl spot. But their start to the season has more weight behind it after beating a good team.

    Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 11:.

    The 49ers have faced the No. 1 defense in DVOA (Seattle) and the No. 1 defense in EPA allowed per play (Minnesota). They scored 32 points against the Seahawks and 35 against the Vikings. They got a defensive touchdown in each game but it seems like no defense can hold down the 49ers this season.

    While the offense has been fantastic, the 49ers wouldn't be the best team in football through Week 11 without their defense, which has excelled despite Nick Bosa not having a sack all season (he did have two quarterback hits on Sunday night). The 49ers have given up 17 or fewer points in six of their 10 games. They have given up fewer than 300 yards in six games too. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who replaced Robert Saleh, is doing an excellent job.

    In a recent development, the Bills have given up 37 points in four games since their bye. Of course, they have faced an incredibly fortunate run of backup quarterbacks, including Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Cade Klubnik (who replaced an injured Geno Smith in the second half) and Kyle McCord. Still, they have not given up a touchdown in 43 straight drives, the longest streak during a season since the 2019 Patriots, according to the Bills' site. That makes the Thanksgiving primetime matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs one that will help shape this NFL season. Is the Bills' defensive improvement real or because of facing inept quarterbacks?

    In a recent development, the Bills' defense struggled early, allowing at least 29 points in five of Buffalo's first six games. The only team to not reach 29 points was the Chargers, who are right now 1-9. But the Bills felt like they weren't far off.

    Industry observers note that "When teams were scoring on us, I felt like we were playing good ball," Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau said, via the team's site. "We just had to clean up a couple things here and there. We were playing good ball. We weren't really finishing games at the end of the games.".

    The Bears haven't trailed in five straight games, and that streak brings back memories of the greatest team in franchise history. The last time the Bears went five games without trailing was 1985, when they went the final three games of the regular season and the first two playoff games without trailing, according to Larry Mayer of ChicagoBears.com. The Bears briefly trailed the Patriots 3-0 in Super Bowl XX before winning 46-10.

    According to recent reports, while this version of the Bears is much different than the famous 1985 team, their pass rush is starting to emerge since Jeffery Simmons came aboard in a trade. On Sunday, they sacked the Saints' Tyler Shough six times (three times by Simmons) and had 24 pressures, which is the most for the team since 2018, according to Next Gen Stats. The defensive improvement will be tested on Thanksgiving in a massive NFC North game against the Lions.

    Industry observers note that very good teams are allowed to lose games, even ones in which they're favored. But the teams now ahead of them in the rankings haven't taken many losses, and now the Jaguars have three after a miserable performance in a defeat to the Giants on Sunday. Their chances to get the No. 1 seed in the AFC dropped to 1.6% after Sunday, according to DVOA.

    In a recent development, the Jaguars can rightfully complain that a questionable call cost Parker Washington a touchdown. But the offensive issues for the first three quarters are what ultimately cost them the game. The Jaguars, whose offense had been very good before Sunday, had just one drive longer than 23 yards in the first three quarters and didn't score a touchdown. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen took responsibility, saying his strategy "maybe had too many things in, moving parts.".

    "That's a direct reflection of me, and making sure that these guys are prepared well enough," Coen said, via the team's site. "We had been prepared in the majority of our football games, I felt like, and that did not show tonight, especially early on. I put that directly on me.".

    The Chiefs scored on all five of their first-half drives against the Cardinals, swiftly putting away a poor and injured team. One of the stars of the game was tight end Travis Kelce, who is having a remarkable season at age 37. He has 586 yards and four touchdowns, two of which came Sunday against Arizona. His 58.6 yards per game is his most since 2023. There were only three instances of a tight end having more than 400 yards at age 37, and Kelce is already second on that list behind Tony Gonzalez and his 859 yards in 2013. Kelce is on pace for 996 yards.

    Sources indicate that there were conversations that Kelce could retire after each of the past two seasons, but he's still one of the most productive tight ends in the game. That helps a Chiefs offense that is fourth in EPA per play.

    According to recent reports, it was a typical Broncos win and not the blowout the 38-24 score indicates. They were outgained 370-351 by the Raiders. Las Vegas rallied to tie the game at 17 after falling behind 17-0 and had the ball at the two-minute warning, down seven points. A pick-6 by Ja'Quan McMillian put the game away in the Broncos' favor.

    The best part of the win for the Broncos was perhaps finding an offensive identity. Rookie Jonah Coleman has taken over the backfield, and he had 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 rushing attempts Sunday.

    "It's not easy, but he's responded really well to his situation," quarterback Bo Nix said, according to the team's transcripts. "He's been given a great opportunity with RJ Harvey getting hurt (knee) and having a few weeks off. ... It was an impressive performance getting that many carries, running the ball hard.".

    It has been revealed that the Bengals have leaned into being a one-dimensional offense, and it hurt them Monday in a road loss to the Commanders. Washington got consistent pressure on Joe Burrow, including on some well-timed blitzes, and that was partly because it didn't have to worry about Cincinnati's running game. The Bengals rushed 14 times for 31 yards and threw it 40 times. When the Bengals got into field-goal range in the final two minutes, they couldn't run for a first down to grind out the remainder of the clock. They passed on second and third downs and couldn't pick it up. That allowed the Commanders 46 seconds, which they used to drive for a game-winning field goal.

    According to recent reports, the Bengals should lean on Burrow, who is still tracking to win an MVP after 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. But the lack of a running game, and even the lack of any attempt to try it, could be a big problem for the Bengals in the playoffs.

    Detroit's first defensive test without Aidan Hutchinson went well. The Lions allowed just 274 yards and 21 points, and Tampa Bay got 65 yards and a touchdown on a meaningless drive at the end of a game when Detroit led by 17 points. The Lions had four sacks, which was a good sign. The Lions' defense has been much better since the first few weeks of the season, and Sunday's game was without Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell.

    The test Thursday will be tougher, with the Chicago Bears coming in with first place in the NFC North on the line. But if Detroit's defense can maintain this level, the Lions might be a Super Bowl contender. That could reveal itself on Thanksgiving.

    It has been revealed that "Our guys are competitive, man, and they don't want to be counted out," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said of the defense's performance Sunday, via the team's site. "And nobody cares. There are no excuses. And the only way to gain respect is just go about your business, man, and make plays and play together and prove your worth, man.".

    Recent findings suggest that what we learned about the Vikings on Sunday night, mostly, was that the 49ers are on a much different tier. That's OK, because the 49ers are on a higher tier than all but a few teams.

    The blitz was impervious to the 49ers' offense. Minnesota blitzed on 88.9% of San Francisco's dropbacks, and Brock Purdy was 19-of-23 passing for 231 yards and two touchdowns on those plays, according to Pro Football Focus.

    "It's one of those things where I told our team, you know, when you play a good team like that and you don't play your best, you're going to get beat," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell stated, according to the team's site.

    That hadn't happened before to the Vikings' defense and is unlikely to repeat, but now Minnesota has to adjust after its worst defensive day of the season.

    Industry observers note that the NFC West race is probably over, with the 49ers leading it by three games, but Seattle has a shot to make it interesting. The Seahawks play at the 49ers in Week 12 and there's an opportunity to at least make the race interesting.

    The substantial story will be Sam Darnold, whether he can return from injury and how well he plays. The Seahawks are not entertaining the idea of replacing him with Drew Lock. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald defended Darnold, pointing out that he has been injured for most of the season, starting with the first game.

    Sources indicate that "The beginning of the year for Sam has been a tough road," Macdonald noted on Seattle Sports 710, via the team's site. "I can't wait for him to be fully healthy, probably for the first time — minimal times it's happened this year — and get a full week's worth of work and we'll rock and roll from there.".

    The dream of getting Puka Nacua back for a playoff run is dead, after Nacua had knee surgery that will keep him out the rest of the season. Davante Adams should return but the Rams' offense won't be what was expected before the season, when expectations were sky high.

    Even making the playoffs will be difficult because of the Rams' challenging upcoming schedule. Their playoff odds are down to 38.1%, according to DVOA. The Rams practically need a win Wednesday over the Packers, who are one of their main competitors in a very tough NFC wild-card race.

    Micah Parsons is set to return for the Packers after practicing in pads Sunday. It's major news for Green Bay to add one of the NFL's best players to the lineup. The Packers were 9-3-1 and leading in the second half at Denver when Parsons tore his ACL last season.

    According to recent reports, wednesday at the Rams is a massive game for the Packers and their playoff hopes, and there will be the temptation to play Parsons more than he's ready for in his return. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is aware of that issue.

    "I never wanna place limitations on anybody, but he hasn't played football in a long time," LaFleur noted, via Athlon Sports. "So, I think you've got to be conscious of that, and there's probably going to be plays that don't look like him, and there's going to be some plays that do.".

    It has been revealed that perhaps the biggest development for the Giants on Sunday was defensive end Abdul Carter picking up two sacks. Production had been surprisingly thin for the third overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft. He had just six sacks in 26 games before Sunday, though his underlying metrics said that sacks were bound to come. Carter also had five quarterback hits.

    Carter came in as an elite prospect and if he can start translating his pass rush success into sacks, that could be huge for the Giants. That happened Sunday as the defense played very well against a good Jaguars offense.

    "As a defense, we showed what we really about," Carter told CBS after the game. "And for me, I'm the best in the world.".

    Sources indicate that seeing the Raiders' upset bid fall short was good news for the Browns. Their game against Las Vegas in Week 12, which got flexed to Sunday night, would have been much more interesting in the wild-card race had the Raiders been 5-6 instead of 4-7. It also wasn't bad for Cleveland to see the Steelers slip back to 6-4 with a bad loss at Philadelphia.

    The Browns aren't a lock to make the playoffs but the path is very clear. They have two games left against the Bengals and one against the Giants, but the other four are against teams with losing records.

    The biggest game in the NFC South this season comes in Tampa Bay next Monday night. The Panthers face the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay gets the season sweep and the tiebreaker with the win. The Falcons and Saints aren't completely out of the running, but Carolina and Tampa Bay look like the two best teams in a bad division.

    In a recent development, an old problem popped up again, and it was the run defense. Baltimore had 157 rushing yards, averaging 7.1 yards per attempt. That's a bad weakness to have against the Buccaneers, who lead the NFL at 5 yards per carry.

    Sources indicate that "They had way too many yards today. Takeaways and stuff is cool, but we got to stop them in the run game," linebacker Tyrel Dodson told the team's site.

    In a recent development, the Steelers were showing improvement but the last two weeks are alarming. They were destroyed by the Bengals, then didn't threaten an Eagles team that had lost seven in a row and was on its third quarterback this season. The lingering problem from the game is receiver DK Metcalf getting ejected after another unproductive game. The NFL reportedly won't suspend him, but that doesn't mean Pittsburgh can rely on a player who hasn't done much on the field and whose behavior is unreliable too.

    There are also injury concerns at a key spot. Edge rusher Nick Herbig was inactive Sunday because of rib and hip injuries, then Alex Highsmith left the game against the Eagles early because of an ankle injury. The Steelers get the 8-2 Broncos on Friday and the Texans and Jaguars after that. Pittsburgh was once 6-2. It's possible it will be under .500 by mid-December.

    David Montgomery could finally make a big impact for the Texans. In his return from injury, he rushed for 107 yards on 26 carries against the Colts. Indianapolis isn't a good team but it was still nice to see something positive from Houston's running game, even if it was in a blowout.

    The Texans have been looking for consistency all season, but it's not too late for them to rally for a wild-card spot in a weak race. Their Week 13 game at the Steelers will be a massive one for the Texans' playoff hopes. For now, Houston hopes a dominant win over Indianapolis is the start of a streak.

    "It's huge," quarterback C.J. Stroud said, according to the team's site. "I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with.".

    Jayden Daniels is still capable of looking like a superstar at quarterback. When the Commanders looked like they had lost to the Bengals on a field goal with 46 seconds left, Daniels hit two passes to rookie Antonio Williams for a total of 64 yards, which set up a game-winning field goal as time expired. They were two great throws from Daniels and a great job by Williams to get open. Daniels finished with 289 yards, 122 of which went to Williams.

    Industry observers note that the Commanders remain two games behind the Giants in the NFC East. But Daniels and Williams kept the Commanders' season alive with two great plays in the final minute on Monday night.

    Recent findings suggest that baker Mayfield's injuries have played a big part in his quiet season, but the Buccaneers still need more from the passing game. Mayfield's top game this season is 243 yards. He had 187 yards against a vulnerable Lions defense on Sunday. Mayfield has just five passing touchdowns in 175 attempts. His yards per attempt of 6.3 is the lowest of his career.

    Industry observers note that mayfield was playing through a foot injury Sunday. The Buccaneers need more out of the passing game because they can't keep dropping games and stay in the NFC South race. A loss Monday night to the Panthers might ruin their playoff hopes.

    "We're out of mulligans," Mayfield remarked, according to the team's site.

    Sources indicate that it's weird to say after giving up 30 points at home to the Titans, but the Cowboys' defense looked better after Mike Pettine took over play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Almost all of the Titans' yards came when they were down double digits and trying to get back in the game. The Titans didn't score a touchdown in the first half.

    Industry observers note that "Very proud of those guys," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer mentioned of the defense, according to the team's site. "I think the first half was outstanding, but I thought they did a great job of blocking out the noise and working. I was really excited for how they performed.".

    Fernando Mendoza played well, although his pick-6 in the fourth quarter with the game on the line was a rookie moment. Against a very good Broncos defense, Mendoza had 267 passing yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed for 22 yards. He played well despite being without superstar tight end Brock Bowers, who was out with an ankle injury. For a second NFL start, it was promising.

    Industry observers note that "He's a first-round pick, first overall for a reason," Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton said, via the team's transcripts. "He's going to be a good player.".

    The pick-6 just after the two-minute warning ended the Raiders' comeback hopes. There was still progress from Mendoza.

    It has been revealed that "I felt a lot more comfortable this week than last week," Mendoza said, via the team's site. "They're both great defenses, both top in the league. However, I just felt like I was able to settle in and was able to see the entire field better. I was able to see the entire football field.".

    Daniel Jones could remain an option for the Patriots after he was suddenly released by the Colts, though head coach Mike Vrabel wouldn't address that Monday. He said Tommy DeVito will start in Week 12.

    "We're excited about that, good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said.

    It has been revealed that deVito struggled when he was forced into action against the Lions in Germany before the bye week. He gets to face the Chargers this weekend, which gives DeVito a chance to impress and keep the job. But it also wouldn't be surprising if Jones finishes the season for a Patriots team that is still in the playoff race.

    Years from now, people will look back on the 2026 Ravens, see that Lamar Jackson missed most of the season and attribute Baltimore's poor record to that. And it won't be completely accurate. The defense, which is head coach Jesse Minter's specialty, has been miserable.

    Over the Ravens' last five games they have allowed 35, 36, 33, 23 and 35 points. Baltimore lost all five of those games, and its losing streak is at six. Minter took the blame for the Panthers putting together a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, saying "It was just a poor job by me, and that's what it was." Players disagreed.

    Recent findings suggest that "I wouldn't necessarily agree with it, truthfully," linebacker Roquan Smith told the team's site. "I thought we were in some really good calls. It comes down to us doing our job. That has been the story all season.".

    It has been revealed that the responsibility for a bad season still falls on Minter, who is in his first season as a head coach. Baltimore is 26th in the NFL in points allowed.

    It has been revealed that the Saints really don't do anything well. They're 21st in points scored per game and 22nd in yards gained, 23rd in points allowed and 27th in yards allowed. They're 16th in passing yards, 18th in passing yards allowed, 28th in rushing yards and 28th in rushing yards allowed. Even the passing yardage is not that great; Tyler Shough's yards per attempt of 6.2 is better than only four of the 32 qualified quarterbacks this season. Up and down their résumé, nothing stands out as a strength.

    It has been revealed that it has been a dreadful follow-up to a good second half to last season, which provided false hope for the Saints heading into this season. It looks like a multiple-year rebuild is still in the beginning stages. The good news is the Saints would have the eighth overall pick of the draft if the season ended now.

    It has been revealed that the problem with the Falcons isn't even their record because they play in the NFC South. But their upcoming schedule is at Vikings, vs. Lions and at Browns. Even one win in those three puts them at 4-9 with four to go. Atlanta will have to play a lot better to stay alive in the playoff hunt over the next three games.

    The Falcons had a great two-game stretch against the Packers and Saints and also are the only team to beat the 49ers, so figuring out why they can't play that way most weeks has been tough.

    Recent findings suggest that "We got really good players, man," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson remarked, via the team's site. "Obviously, with the good players, you have to execute at a high level. We have to come together this week and tell ourselves, 'Is this how we want to end the season?'".

    Industry observers note that sunday wasn't perfect for the Eagles, with just 214 yards on offense, but their defense is starting to play well. It allowed 255 yards in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, the second straight time the Eagles have held an opponent under 300 yards. Before that stretch, the Eagles hadn't held an opponent to fewer than 300 yards since Week 2, which was the last time Philadelphia had won a game before Sunday.

    The Eagles will be tested against a very good Cowboys offense that is coming off a 51-point game against the Titans. But seeing the defense come through, with stellar linebacker play from Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell, gives them hope for a happy Thanksgiving.

    In a recent development, the Jets have little to play for, and a loss to the Chargers would have put them in much better draft position next April, but winning is good for any NFL locker room. Even if it's against the Chargers.

    "The thing is, a win is a win and that's what we look for and that's the way you play this game," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said, according to the team's site.

    There have been some promising developments in the Jets' season, and probably none bigger than the play of edge rusher David Bailey, the second overall pick of the draft. Bailey had two more sacks, giving him 9.5 for the season. Jevon Kearse set the rookie record with 14.5 and Bailey is on pace to break that, though in a 17-game season. He has been undeniably impressive and a significant piece for a Jets team that has three first-round picks next year.

    Nick Rallis always seemed like an awkward fit as the Cardinals' defensive coordinator, considering he wasn't successful in three previous seasons under an old regime but was retained. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur fired him Monday after another disappointing performance. The Cardinals are 31st in expected points added allowed per play, ahead of only the Cowboys.

    According to recent reports, the Cardinals haven't been good on defense, but talent certainly seems to be lacking. Safety Budda Baker, the one star the defense has, leads the team with 3.5 sacks. That's a terrible sign. First-round picks up front, like Zaven Collins and Darius Robinson, haven't broken out. We're about to find out if that was because of a coaching problem.

    It has been revealed that the Colts cutting Daniel Jones less than 24 hours after his 11th straight start to begin the season was odd, even if it ensures they don't have to pay a 2027 injury guarantee. Jones was poor against the Texans, but he was poor all season. He's dead last among NFL starting quarterbacks in EPA per play this season. But the Colts didn't care before Week 11, starting Jones and seemingly never giving any serious consideration to benching him to at least get a look at Anthony Richardson Sr. Cutting a quarterback after starting him all season is a sign of a franchise that isn't making sound decisions.

    At least the Colts now can get a look at Richardson, who indicated some progress in the preseason. Richardson hasn't shown many signs that he can be an NFL starter, but it's not like the Colts are losing anything by taking another look.

    According to recent reports, the Dolphins haven't been dominated often. They were dominated Sunday, when they fell behind early and got crushed by a superior Bills team.

    According to recent reports, one positive point from Sunday was another major game from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, who had 13 tackles and an interception. He has 93 tackles, a pair of interceptions and a sack this season. Rodriguez was a tremendous college player but he fell to the second round of the NFL Draft. He has already shown that his production at Texas Tech was no fluke and gives the Dolphins one foundational piece in what is going to be a long rebuild.

    There wasn't much to be happy with after Sunday's blowout loss. Cam Ward's final line didn't look terrible, but in the first half against a Cowboys defense that is worst in the NFL in many categories, Ward had 55 passing yards and the Titans didn't score a touchdown.

    The defense was even worse, giving up 51 points. In Tennessee's last four games it has allowed 491, 510, 459 and 480 yards. The defense was supposed to be much better under head coach Robert Saleh, and it is one of the worst in the NFL. Tennessee has allowed more yards per game than any other team.

    "These last couple of weeks, I'm not going to try and sugarcoat anything," Saleh said Monday, according to the team's site. "It's been dog s***.".

    According to recent reports, good thing the Chargers got that win in Week 10. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again.

    At least there were a couple of decent performances on offense. Omarion Hampton continued to get hot late in the season with 89 rushing yards. Justin Herbert had a 119.3 passer rating. His best mark in a game this season before Sunday was 87.5. Unfortunately, Herbert landed in concussion protocol after the loss. Ladd McConkey has had an injury-filled and unproductive season but he had two touchdowns against the Jets. It's not much, especially in a loss. But it's not like there have been many other positives for the Chargers.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • China is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S.
    • China Economic and Security Review Commission report said Beijing is applying military, economic, maritime, and other forms of pressure to constrain India.
    • China has recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India's electronics manufacturing, slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants, and imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry, the report noted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    China is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.

    On Nov. 18, a U.S. China Economic and Security Review Commission report said Beijing is applying military, economic, maritime, and other forms of pressure to constrain India.

    China has recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India's electronics manufacturing, slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants, and imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry, the report noted.

    It added that these tensions offer the U.S. an opportunity to counter growing Chinese influence by building closer ties with India across key sectors such as pharmaceutical and defense.

    Ties have improved since a deadly border skirmish in 2020, but experts told CNBC that trust is still thin between Beijing and New Delhi. However, they added that the uneasy peace with China is unlikely to make India align automatically with the U.S. as an ally.

    The Indian foreign and commerce ministries and the Chinese foreign ministry did not respond to emails seeking comments.

    The thawing in relations between India and China came amid industrial demand, as well as the need for "a whole lot of posturing for the U.S.," stated Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo.

    In a recent development, over the past year, India faced tariff pressures and needed to signal to Washington that its options remain open, including that of renegotiating relations with China, he explained, but added that as the trade deal with the U.S. is "close enough now," there is no pressing need for that signaling.

    Further improvement in the relationship is also limited by reports of renewed border tensions between the two sides and Beijing's scant reciprocation on easing access to technology and people movement, he said.

    Last month, an Indian military official noted that confrontations with Chinese soldiers were ongoing across several locations along the country's northeastern border, even as top leaders from the countries met with fanfare at the BRICS Summit in September.

    Sources indicate that another flash point was when Beijing put export controls on tunnel boring machines last month. "Our relations with China remain good, and if there aren't any new hurdles, they can improve further," India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal reportedly noted after China's move to tighten TBM exports.

    On Monday, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson reportedly said Beijing is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides amid reports that fewer Indian businessmen got visas to attend an annual trade fair in Shanghai.

    The Chinese "actively disrupt" areas where India is trying to make progress in terms of moving global supply chains, developing advanced industrial technologies such as EVs, batteries, electronic components, and pharmaceutical ingredients, Pramit Pal Chaudhuri, South Asia practice head at Eurasia Group, told CNBC.

    He added China is increasingly focused on containing India economically rather than through military overtures.

    According to recent reports, india's manufacturing push still relies on Chinese inputs, from electronics components and solar materials to rare earth magnets and specialized machinery. Between April and October, India imported goods worth $96.6 billion from China, up more than 30% from a year ago, as per commerce ministry data released earlier this month.

    Its major imports from China include electronic goods, machinery, chemicals, transport equipment, iron and steel, and pharmaceutical products.

    While India needs inputs for its manufacturing ambitions from Beijing and China values access to Indian markets, trust between the two sides is "still thin," according to Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft, citing a large trade imbalance and overlapping interests in South Asia and the Indian Ocean as additional challenges.

    Trump administration proposes rule that could curb ESG investing in 401(k)s

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Trump administration proposed a rule on Monday that officials stated they expect to severely cripple so-called ESG investing in workplace retirement aims such as 401(k)s.
    • The proposed regulation, if finalized, would amend provisions under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, or ERISA, to clarify how employers and other plan "fiduciaries" can apply their duty of loyalty to 401(k) investors.
    • According to recent reports, the rule affirms that the people who choose investments for their organization retirement plan must make decisions "solely in the financial interests of workers and retirees, not to advance political or social agendas," U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Trump administration proposed a rule on Monday that officials stated they expect to severely cripple so-called ESG investing in workplace retirement aims such as 401(k)s.

    The proposed regulation, if finalized, would amend provisions under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, or ERISA, to clarify how employers and other plan "fiduciaries" can apply their duty of loyalty to 401(k) investors.

    According to recent reports, the rule affirms that the people who choose investments for their organization retirement plan must make decisions "solely in the financial interests of workers and retirees, not to advance political or social agendas," U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling stated Monday in a written statement.

    In a recent development, ESG — short for environmental, social and governance — funds let people invest according to certain values such as curbing climate change or improving corporate diversity. They're also known as socially responsible, sustainable, impact or values-based funds.

    "We make clear in this rule that when you are selecting investments for a retirement plan ... you may not have any ulterior motives or collateral interests," a Labor Department official noted during a press briefing Monday morning.

    Recent findings suggest that "We believe that will inform all fiduciaries as to whether an impact fund or ESG fund is appropriate for retirement funds," the official said. "We believe the answer will be very rarely.".

    Already, few 401(k) aims offer ESG funds — partly due to whipsawing federal policy around their use.

    According to recent reports, about 5% of 401(k) aims offered an ESG fund in 2025, according to a Strategy Sponsor Council of America report issued earlier this month. On average, less than 1% of overall investor assets in 401(k) plans are held in ESG funds, the report stated.

    The Labor Department proposal, which is subject to a 60-day public comment period, comes as the Trump administration has tried to make it easier for employers to add alternative investments such as private equity funds to workplace retirement aims.

    It also comes amid a broader Trump administration backlash against ESG and policies it views as "woke.".

    It has been revealed that within days of his inauguration in 2025, President Donald Trump announced the U.S. would withdraw from the Paris Agreement, blocked subsidies for electric vehicles, pushed for more fossil-fuel production, and started a "huge pushback" against diversity, equity and inclusion policies, Diana Iovanel, a senior markets economist at Capital Economics, wrote in a research note last year.

    "Our country will be woke no longer," Trump remarked during a speech to a joint session of Congress in March 2025.

    More recently, Trump and the Republican-led Congress repealed key elements of the Inflation Reduction Act, former President Joe Biden's signature law to combat climate change. In April, a White House report mentioned ESG investing has a "significant cost to investors and the broader economy.".

    Recent findings suggest that monday's proposal undoes elements of a Biden administration rule in 2022, Labor Department officials said. That Biden-era regulation sought to loosen ESG investing rules put in place in 2020 by the first Trump administration. The Biden rule, for example, clarified that employers could weigh the economic effects of climate change and other ESG considerations when making investment choices, officials said at the time.

    Among the ways the latest proposal seeks to curb ESG uptake in 401(k) plans is by eliminating the "tiebreaker test" and the "participant preference provision," the Labor Department noted.

    The tiebreaker test says, for example, that if an ESG fund is "tied" with another fund after comparing various financial factors, a 401(k) plan sponsor can choose the ESG fund because of its social benefits, according to legal experts.

    Current rules also allow employers to select funds based partly on their workers' preferences, provided they still meet certain financial criteria.

    Data demonstrates that ESG funds may provide stronger financial performance than that of more traditional funds, however.

    For example, sustainable funds returned investors a median 4.9% in the first half of 2026, versus 4% for traditional funds, according to a Morgan Stanley analysis in September.

    "Sustainable funds also continue to outperform over the long term: A hypothetical $100 investment into a sustainable fund in December 2018 — the start date for Morningstar's sustainable fund classification — would have grown to $171 today, while investing $100 into a traditional fund over the same period of time would have become $159 today, assuming median returns were achieved in each period," according to the report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia confirmed it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.

    The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the company's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers noted.

    In a recent development, "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a China hawk who is retiring from Congress, told CNBC in a phone interview. "To me it's a failure of character.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC in an extended interview later Monday morning that he personally intervened to convince Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, saying, "I made the deal.".

    Bacon, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation, remarked he wants the next Congress to conduct thorough oversight, while questioning the Trump administration's motives.

    "Somebody's responsible for this, and it may be" Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department is responsible for setting U.S. export controls on AI chips, Bacon noted. "But I think we should get to the bottom of this.".

    Huang, who is scheduled to testify before multiple committees on Capitol Hill starting Dec. 1, is "going to get high scrutiny in a bipartisan way when he comes next week," Bacon noted.

    Huang's closed-door appearance before a trio of House committees is on the schedule, as the panels seek answers on the national security implications of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, MS NOW reported. The Senate banking committee announced after Huang's reinstatement that he will appear for a public hearing Dec. 3.

    John Fisher of Trident, a spokesman for Huang, declined to comment on the Nvidia CEO's scheduled appearances.

    "He better be there," Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told CNBC about Huang's scheduled Dec. 1 appearance. His reinstatement will only intensify congressional probes into Nvidia and its government connections, Amo predicted.

    "I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query, and it makes Howard Lutnick and his dealings — supporting his nepo children's operation at Cantor Fitzgerald — party to inquiry as well as any other administration official that has facilitated a status quo in which chips can be sold to China or Chinese operated intermediaries who don't intend good things for the American people," remarked Amo, referring to the financial firm run by Lutnick's sons that has business ties to Nvidia.

    A Cantor spokesperson didn't comment directly when asked about Amo's comments, saying the firm "holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia" and noting its Nvidia positions "arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients.".

    The Commerce Department didn't immediately respond to requests to comment on Bacon's and Amo's remarks.

    Nvidia in a statement Monday mentioned it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    Industry observers note that david Rudenstine, a constitutional law professor and national security scholar at Cardozo School of Law, said the frenzy around Huang's comeback is secondary to lingering national security concerns."The real responsibility for national security is with the administration and not with the CEO of a private company," Rudenstine told CNBC."You're opposed to China getting the chips. You recognize that the intermediary companies are sending chips to China, and you don't put a stop to it. I don't get it," he said.

    The CEO's reinstatement, while celebrated by the White House and in Silicon Valley, led to heightened calls on Capitol Hill to seek answers on AI chip exports to China and what the Trump administration's role has been in facilitating that.

    It has been revealed that "We are sending high-end computer chips to China, and yet we're saying we want to win the AI war. It's a contradiction, and it's a failure of leadership in the White House," Bacon told CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, told CNBC in an emailed statement that Huang's return "proves that under Trump, Vance, and Rubio, national security is for sale to the highest bidder.".

    "We will all pay the price of letting China plunder America's cutting edge technology. Democrats will be pushing for accountability for anyone in the administration that put corrupt deals over our country's security," Wyden, who is also a Senate Intelligence Committee member, remarked.

    Recent findings suggest that trump in a Truth Social post Monday added that Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Lawmakers, who have already rolled out multiple investigations related to Huang, Nvidia and related entities, quickly filed in to question those conclusions.

    In a recent development, sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., a close Trump ally and a former CEO, criticized the move and called for a congressional briefing "as soon as possible" on Huang's reinstatement.

    It has been revealed that "Nvidia's board is free to vote however they want, but the federal government owes the American people answers about what actually happened," Scott told CNBC in an emailed statement. "This looks terrible on its face, and it drives home the need for Congress to be informed on the full impact of Jensen Huang's actions on our national security and economy.".

    Recent findings suggest that rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, told CNBC that it's still not clear to what degree Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy might have compromised national security.

    "The fact that the president of the United States is involved in putting him back in there, presumably because maybe he has stock or he just cares about the stock market, it's really reached a bizarre place," Peters said. "And obviously that man has not learned anything from the election about what people think of him, or he doesn't care.".

    Monday's move also gave fuel to lawmakers who have already questioned Trump, his administration or Nvidia.

    Sources indicate that "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the firm's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement via the Senate Banking Committee, where she is the top Democrat and is expected to become chair in January.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, more tersely questioned the official assurances that Huang poses no risks to national security.

    "No national security risk? Based on what?" he wrote on X.

    Industry observers note that rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., who serves on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, in an X post called Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang "outrageous.".

    "We still don't know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia's own board has completed its investigation," wrote Krishnamoorthi, who is also a member of the House Oversight and Intelligence panels.

    Recent findings suggest that A U.S. appeals court on Monday cleared the Army to proceed with a controlled detonation of nearly five tons of degraded explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant, overturning a bid by environmental groups to block an emergency federal permit for the blast.

    The order clears the way for the Army's proposal to destroy around 68 barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, near the Iowa-Illinois border, on Wednesday.

    A three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied a request by environmental groups seeking to challenge an emergency permit from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency authorizing the operation.

    "We are mindful of the very real risks presented by the Army's planned detonation of the stores of degraded lead azide," the ruling mentioned. "However, we must acknowledge the realities of the situation: the degraded explosives present a risk of an uncontrolled and unplanned explosion, which would occur without the benefit of the safety measures that the Permit puts in place.".

    Industry observers note that the planned blast, originally scheduled for Nov. 20, has been delayed three times amid regional concerns over possible health and environmental effects and criticism that the government failed to adequately communicate the potential risks to local communities.

    It has been revealed that the detonation is expected to produce a dust plume containing lead particles, a toxic metal that can cause serious health effects, according to the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Breathing in lead-containing particles or coming into contact with lead dust deposited on surrounding surfaces could pose potential health risks, the agency said.

    It has been revealed that the U.S. Army has argued that the risk of the material detonating on its own has increased as temperatures fall, and that the explosive compound, stored for more than two decades, has degraded to the point that moving it is too dangerous.

    It has been revealed that president Donald Trump said in a social media post Monday that he had told the Army to hold off until the court weighed in. He added that the decision would be subject to Iowa's Democratic Gov.-elect Rob Sand, who takes office in January, warning that further delay could risk "a large, spontaneous explosion.".

    In an X post late Monday following the court ruling, Sand mentioned the Trump administration "should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks.".

    "Everyday Iowans are entitled to know how Middletown came to this situation, and learn why the administration believes this is the best path forward," Sand remarked, urging the federal government to share information with the public as soon as possible.

    Industry observers note that in remarks consistent with previous statements, the influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 before hitting the goal the following year.
