    Maikel Garcia trade grades: Mariners land Gold Glove infielder; Royals get pitching help, but with huge risks

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1270 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade.
    • Garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense.
    • Industry observers note that the 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Mariners have acquired third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade, the teams announced on Wednesday. The Royals receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller and lefty Jose A. Ferrer in the deal.

    Here are the full trade details:.

    Garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense. He is a year removed from a 5.6 WAR season and receiving MVP votes. Garcia is signed long-term as well. He's owed a very reasonable $52.5 million through 2030, with a club option for 2031.

    Industry observers note that the 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City. An oblique strain delayed the start to his 2026 season, but once healthy, he threw 118 ⅔ innings with a 4.17 ERA and under-the-hood numbers that were hit (3.70 expected ERA) or miss (4.41 FIP). Miller threw 180 ⅓ innings with a 2.94 ERA in 2024, and will remain under team control through 2029.

    Ferrer, 26, is a workhorse ground ball reliever with three years of control remaining. McArthur (fracture) and Evans (Tommy John) both missed 2026 with elbow surgery. McArthur pitched in four minor-league rehab games in September and should be ready for spring training. Evans has surgery in January and is expected back at midseason.

    Here now are our grades for this three-for-three swap between 2027 American League postseason hopefuls.

    The Mariners came into the offseason with an opening at third base, a glaring need to improve their defense, and more starters than rotation spots. That all came to a head in this trade. They used Miller, their least effective starter the last two seasons, and two spare parts to net a long-term solution at the hot corner in Garcia, who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense.

    One player alone won't fix Seattle's defense, of course, but Garcia is a very major step toward improving a unit that ranked 26th in defensive runs saved and 30th (by a lot) in outs above average. As for the lineup, upcoming manager Jason Kanzler can run out something like this most days:.

    Industry observers note that donovan was limited to 39 games by two groin strains and a concussion this past season. He's very versatile and needn't be locked into DH. The Mariners can play Donovan in the outfield to open up DH at-bats for slugger Lazaro Montes, who hit some titanic home runs during his MLB debut in 2026. They could also move Donovan around to give others DH days.

    Industry observers note that the lineup and the defense are improved, and the Mariners still have a formidable rotation that includes Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, and Bryan Woo. Right-hander Ryan Sloan, arguably the top pitching prospect in baseball (it's either Sloan or Anderson), is knocking on the door and figures to debut at some point in 2027.

    According to recent reports, seattle will miss Ferrer in their bullpen but also have close to an entire offseason (minus a lockout) to replace him. Assuming the Mariners won't break the bank for Adrian Morejon, the free agent market still offers solid second- and third-tier lefty reliever options in A.J. Minter, Sean Newcomb, JoJo Romero, Gregory Soto, and Alex Vesia. Ferrer is a quality reliever but not irreplaceable.

    Before his elbow fracture, which ultimately required three surgeries, McArthur demonstrated a very lively curveball and strong ground ball ability. He's a middle reliever more than a high-leverage option, but is not merely a throw-in. Langevin struck out 106 batters in 55 ⅓ Single-A relief innings thanks to his mid-90s fastball in 2026. He also walked 39 batters, however.

    Sources indicate that garcia received MVP votes a year ago thanks to a .286/.351/.449 line with 16 home runs and 23 stolen bases. He also runs some of the game's best contact rates. That's his upside and maybe 2025 was a career year, but Garcia has a reasonably high floor thanks to his defense. Getting even league-average offense moving forward makes this a win for Seattle.

    The free agent market is flush with No. 3-4 type starters and light on position players, specifically non-first base infielders. Couldn't the Royals keep Garcia and just sign a pitcher or two? There is something to be said for Miller's cost control as an arbitration-eligible player, of course, but he hasn't been healthy and effective at the same time since 2024. That's awfully risky.

    It has been revealed that evans is a quality second piece as long as he bounces back well from Tommy John surgery. He made his MLB debut with the Mariners in 2025 and underwhelmed (4.32 ERA with iffy underlying numbers in 81 ⅓ innings), though he was regarded as a strong prospect before that, someone who should hold down a rotation spot for a long time.

    Here's what FanGraphs wrote about Evans in June 2025, the last time he was prospect-eligible:.

    Industry observers note that (His) sweeper is easily his best pitch, spins in at 2,800 rpm, and has hellacious lateral wipe. His reliance on it robs it of some bat-missing ability, and the last couple of years, the miss rate on Evans' slider has been pretty average because he's so often trying to throw it for strikes and hitters anticipate its arrival. But because Evans' fastball is fairly vulnerable, he's forced to lean on his breaking stuff ... Again, it's really only the sweeper that's plus, but Evans has a super deep repertoire, he throws a good rate of strikes and gets groundballs, and in 2024, he proved he could sustain this kind of stuff across more than 100 innings. Without a single pitch generating plus miss, he's probably not going to be a star, but he does enough to be a useful member of a massive league rotation in a no. 4/5 capacity.

    The Royals will have to wait for Evans to make an impact in their uniform because the timing of his Tommy John surgery means his rehab will extend into next spring and summer, but he is a quality second piece even if he is only a No. 4-5 starter. Cheap back-end starters are incredibly valuable and Evans should be that once his elbow is ready to go.

    Ferrer could very well wind up closing games for the Royals this season and is a quality add to the bullpen. For Kansas City, the trade boils down to three things. One, can they keep Miller healthy and get him back to his 2024 form? He's the headliner in the trade and his success is imperative. Two, will Evans turn into a reliable rotation member once his elbow is sound?

    Recent findings suggest that and three, was Nick Loftin's 2026 for real? The Royals believe it was, hence trading Garcia. Loftin, 28, was a Gold Glove finalist this past season and he authored a .240/.322/.388 batting line with eight home runs in 118 games. If you're sold on Loftin as a league-average hitter and Gold Glove-caliber defender, well, that's what Garcia is, just without the name value.

    Recent findings suggest that the Royals badly needed rotation help -- there's no arguing that -- but they also ranked 22nd in runs this year and were middle of the pack defensively despite Loftin's (and Garcia's) glovework. There's a chance Kansas City made its position player core worse with only unspectacular pitching upgrades to show for it. I understand what they did. I just don't love it.

    #164939. MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal hosts more meetings, Red Sox add backup catcher, plus Padres, Phillies, Rays, more

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1175 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal hosts more meetings, Red Sox add backup catcher, plus Padres, Phillies, Rays, more

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1175 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the hot stove is starting to heat up.
    • According to recent reports, we're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up.
    • The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team declared on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

    According to recent reports, we're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the notable offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

    The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team declared on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

    According to recent reports, fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a big dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

    Industry observers note that the Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

    It has been revealed that skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are stated to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

    Star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

    Seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

    On Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

    San Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

    Recent findings suggest that after signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow said it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

    Breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster issues remaining this offseason.

    Sources indicate that free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

    Although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

    The Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. Kerkering struggled badly in the second half, allowing 25 runs and 43 baserunners in his final 19 ⅓ MLB innings of the season. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

    It has been revealed that still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

    Industry observers note that veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

    Pitching is always in demand, especially cheap pitching with upside behind league-average innings. Montas, 34 in March, has not been healthy and effective at the same time since 2022, though he looked good during his showcase and he has a reputation for being an excellent teammate who mentors young pitchers. That will only help his case.

    Industry News: Sonny Gray returns to Twins on two-year, $55 million contract, per report

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota.
    • Skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray!
    • Gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday announced they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the Upcoming York Post.

    Skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57.

    Gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

    In a recent development, CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:.

    Industry observers note that gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, massive movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

    Gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

    The Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday remarked club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a fresh collective bargaining agreement.
    • "I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred stated while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in New York, via the Athletic.
    • It has been revealed that "Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred said later during a news conference at MLB headquarters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday remarked club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a fresh collective bargaining agreement. While Manfred noted there was general room for compromise with the MLBPA, that does not extend to the central matter of the capped system owners want.

    "I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred stated while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in New York, via the Athletic.

    It has been revealed that "Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred said later during a news conference at MLB headquarters. "I'm not in a position to speculate about what happens in the event that we don't achieve our overriding objective, which is to get a cap and floor system that addresses the competitive problem that our fans perceive.".

    According to recent reports, it's possible to parse "can't imagine" as a subtle rhetorical hedge. Additionally, Manfred before he was commissioner was the league's lead negotiator. As such, he's quite familiar with the appearance of unyielding resolve as a tactical implement. Thus, the league has tied every other proposed change to the players' acceptance of a cap and floor, and the players through their union have historically shown zero willingness to accept such a system.

    "There can be no clearer example of the league's lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts," MLBPA interim head Bruce Meyer said Wednesday in a statement.

    In a recent development, "There should be no illusions about the owners' true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.".

    Industry observers note that in their most recent substantive proposal to the players, MLB pitched a $258.3 million cap and $180.2 million floor on team payrolls, with those limits to be phased in gradually. Back in June, the league proposed a $245.3 million cap and $171.2 million floor.

    It has been revealed that the current CBA, which is the accord that governs every aspect of the working relationship between players and clubs in MLB, is set to expire just before midnight on Dec. 1. At that point, the league is expected to lock out the players at the behest of team owners. The lockout will likely not end until a fresh CBA is agreed to, at least in principle. Owners also locked out the players in 2021, and that lockout lasted 99 days and very nearly ate into the 2022 regular-season schedule.

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    According to recent reports, that made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    It has been revealed that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    You can't make the playoffs in 10 games, but you can definitely give yourself some breathing room when the inevitable ebbs and flows of the season strike. That's exactly what the Boston Bruins have done as they've stood out for the right reasons in a deep Atlantic Division.

    Boston currently leads the division with 15 points, and while the Tampa Bay Lightning's record is technically better, the Bruins' plus-14 goal differential is tied for second in the NHL.

    The biggest reason for this fast start has been the play of Jeremy Swayman in goal. He's allowed one or fewer goals in half of his starts, and Swayman's 8.02 goals saved above average ranks second to old Beantown running mate Linus Ullmark, per Natural Stat Trick.

    We have a long way to go before we start discussing Vezina Trophy candidates seriously, but Swayman certainly has the potential to carry Boston to the postseason.

    Recent findings suggest that it helps that David Pastrnak is an elite playmaker, and the Bruins have been getting contributions from young forwards Fraser Minten and James Hagens. Morgan Geekie has also gone from goal-scoring machine to distributor with seven assists in 10 games.

    It has been revealed that the Atlantic Division will be a heavyweight brawl throughout the season, but to this point, the Bruins have proven to be a worthy combatant. With that in mind, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    #164920. MLB rumors: Mets to meet with NPB star, plus latest on Ketel Marte, Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1219 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    MLB rumors: Mets to meet with NPB star, plus latest on Ketel Marte, Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball.
    • Sources indicate that in theory, there sure is.
    • It's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball. We've seen an All-Star pitcher sign (Sonny Gray to the Twins) and a trade involving an All-Star (Maikel Garcia to the Mariners). The White Sox also signed a mid-rotation starter while the Red Sox grabbed a first baseman fresh off a World Series title. Is there enough time for a flurry of moves before the owners lock the players out when the CBA expires on Dec. 1?

    Sources indicate that in theory, there sure is. We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.

    It's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. A major hurdle might be his 10-and-5 no-trade rights and questions about which teams Marte would approve in a potential deal. Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are said to be interested.

    Marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some complications arose in 2026, including several no-shows. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage.

    It has been revealed that the Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the New York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious.

    Taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023.

    According to recent reports, CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:.

    According to recent reports, listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu declared on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.

    Because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.

    For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

    The Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic.

    Recent findings suggest that sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power.

    CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:.

    He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.

    In a recent development, after being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.

    Further, he also remarked the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season.

    Fresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.

    Recent findings suggest that though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better.

    In a recent development, the Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi.

    Bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings.

    The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons.

    Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

    • Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.
    • The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).
    • However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.

    The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).

    However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.

    It’s reassuring that links to Lamine Camara (who came close to a switch to Chelsea in the summer) have resurfaced ahead of the winter, given ongoing concerns over how Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch fit in an Andoni Iraola side.

    While the performances of Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni have undoubtedly mitigated matters, the truth of the matter is that Liverpool can’t look to rely on the latter of the duo throughout an entire campaign.

    The Reds must, and no doubt will, look after the teenager to ensure his excellent development carries on smoothly, but his recent comments are a clear reminder that investment midway through the campaign is a necessity.

    “I’ve been playing like a number six. I played there when I was young but, to be honest, it’s a newly introduced position for me. I’ve had to learn a lot in a short space of time,” Nyoni told The Inside Scoop (via BBC Sport).

    “I enjoy playing like a six because I can get on the ball and always try to play forwards, but I enjoy playing as an eight as well.

    “I like to drop in, get the ball and play forward but I’ve had to learn the discipline of being a number six.

    “Right now, I don’t really have a preference. As I’m starting out, I enjoy playing both.”.

    We have faith that Iraola’s demands will eventually click with Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, but it’s still painful to see how open Liverpool look in the middle of the park when Mac Allister is forced to share space with either of his senior midfield partners. And the less noted about a double pivot consisting of the Dutchman and the Hungarian, the better.

    Yes, it’s fair to point out that our season is far from spiralling under Iraola — the Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table with only four points standing between them and Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Brighton in second.

    But it does feel like there is an opportunity for Liverpool to make a modest statement in 2026/27. Not quite title glory, it has to be remarked, but certainly to stake a claim as “best of the rest” and set a promising foundation for the seasons to come under Iraola.

    Adding an additional midfielder (like, cough cough, Lamine Camara, cough cough) to the ranks who can carry out the Basque’s demands would undoubtedly serve that purpose.

    According to recent reports, elsewhere, the backline looks in fine shape and the forward line evidently needs time to gel. Give the manager the tools he needs in midfield and this could be an impressive opening campaign for Andoni Iraola.

    #164914. Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin.
    • Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners.
    • The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin. The White Sox are sending Castillo and Martin to the Colorado Rockies for lefty Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz, the teams declared late Thursday. The Rockies will take on Castillo's entire contract.

    Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners. He struggled badly after the deal, allowing 30 runs in 31 innings, and he finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder glitch. Castillo has one year remaining on his contract at $22.75 million, though a $25 million option for 2028 will vest if he throws 150 innings in 2027.

    The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half. The White Sox kept him at arm's length in the postseason despite running bullpen games almost nightly. Martin allowed two runs in one inning in his only postseason appearance.

    Neither Sullivan nor Veliz are significant prospects. For all intents and purposes, the White Sox are attaching Martin to Castillo as a sweetener to get the Rockies to take Castillo's salary. The Rockies are essentially buying Martin, who is under team control through 2030, by taking on the rest of Castillo's contract.

    Here now are our trade grades for this two-for-two swap.

    Fair or not, I'm going to lump the two Castillo trades together. Chicago stepped out to acquire Castillo at the deadline and absorbed the $30 million or so remaining on his contract to do it. Seranthony Domínguez, who had about $15 million left on his deal, went the other way in the trade, so the White Sox took on about $15 million total, and also gave up a pretty good prospect in Boston Smith.

    Four and a half months later, the White Sox had to give up a steady back-end starter in Martin to clear Castillo's money. They ended up saving about $7 million in 2027 in this series of moves, but it cost them Martin and Smith (and Domínguez), and they had to endure 31 awful innings from Castillo. Unless Sullivan or Veliz hit big, the White Sox took a series of Ls here.

    According to recent reports, credit to president of baseball operations Chris Getz for acknowledging a mistake with Castillo and acting quickly to unload him. It was costly, though. Martin isn't a star, but cheap back-end starters are very valuable. We'll see what Getz & Co. do with the savings. Presumably they'll invest in more pitching. Having to give up Martin to dump Castillo so soon is a stinker, though. Ouch.

    The Rockies need all types of pitching (righty, lefty, starter, reliever, whatever) and it's not often they can convince quality (or even competent) free agents to come to Coors Field. They have to develop their own pitchers or trade for pitching, and in this instance, they took on Castillo's hefty salary to get Martin and his four years of control. Creative, if nothing else.

    There is downside potential too. Martin has run below league-average strikeout rates and middling ground ball rates throughout his career. Pitchers who allow a lot of balls in play -- a lot of balls in play in the air -- are a poor match for Coors Field. It's good the Rockies spent and found a way to add controllable pitching. They just might not have picked the best pitcher.

    After losing 104 games in 2026, there is no such thing as a bad dart throw for the Rockies. It's unlikely they would have been able to spend the $22.75 million on a free agent (at least not without overpaying), so taking on Castillo to get Martin is the next best thing. I like the thinking, even if I don't love Martin's profile in Coors Field.

    Latest Update: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • According to recent reports, hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • It has been revealed that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Newly introduced Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams declared the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    According to recent reports, hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    It has been revealed that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    In a recent development, after trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Latest Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    According to recent reports, for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a latest era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Sources indicate that goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    Industry observers note that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Latest Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Industry observers note that hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    In a recent development, in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    Sources indicate that the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Industry observers note that although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Newly introduced Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    Sources indicate that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    That remarked, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Recent findings suggest that daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his upcoming team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    Industry observers note that if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    According to recent reports, the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, it has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins. First, catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday. Jeffers turned down a multi-year offer from the Twins, according to The Athletic, so he's betting on himself. Betting that he'll at least maintain his free agent stock and get paid next offseason.

    Recent findings suggest that then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million. There's an opt-out after the first year. Gray, 37, finished fifth in the AL Cy Young voting this season and pitched wonderfully for the Twins in 2022 and 2023. He joins a rotation that, on paper, looks like one of the better starting units in the American League.

    Here is Minnesota's rotation depth chart:.

    "I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return. "He had an abundance of options, and given where he's at in his career, I know how notable it is to him. He expressed it quite directly how important it is to win, and this isn't just about having a good season or a winning season. It's about winning and going deep in the playoffs and making a real playoff run.".

    In a recent development, matthews could land in the bullpen next season and that might be his long-term home. His stuff should be well suited to a relief role. Gray makes the rotation better and potentially the bullpen better as well by bumping Matthews to relief. Jeffers accepting the qualifying offer keeps a key middle-of-the-order bat in place. A good week for the Twins, this has been.

    Sources indicate that after a disappointing 77-85 finish this year, Minnesota has already improved significantly in the early days of the offseason. They play in the AL Central. With all due respect, it is not the most imposing division. There's no reason the Twins can't be in the division and wild card races next season. Here now is what's left on Minnesota's offseason to-do list.

    Sources indicate that teams had until 5 p.m. ET Friday to offer their pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players contracts for 2027. They didn't have to sign them Friday, but they had to tender an offer; otherwise, the player immediately became a free agent. Dozens of players were cut loose at the non-tender deadline, as usual, and two players stood out as non-tender candidates for the Twins: Trevor Larnach and Royce Lewis. Larnach was indeed non-tendered, while Lewis was dealt to the Dodgers.

    It's not often a player gets non-tendered after posting a .352 on-base percentage and 120 OPS+, but the writing was on the wall. The Twins had an agreement in place to trade Larnach at the deadline (Astros owner Jim Crane nixed the deal) and they have a very crowded outfield. Also, Larnach had wrist surgery earlier this month. That created some questions going into next season, and the Twins opted to cut him loose.

    According to recent reports, larnach had one more year of control remaining and was expected to make over $6 million through arbitration in 2027. I reckon the Twins tried again to trade him prior to Friday's non-tender deadline. In the end, he was non-tendered rather than risk tying $6 million or so up in yet another outfielder, particularly one who is coming off wrist surgery.

    Industry observers note that things got so bad this summer that Lewis, who has a .288 on-base percentage in over 1,200 plate appearances the last three years, was sent to Triple-A for a spell, and also moved across the diamond from third base to first base. The Twins could not count on him to provide offense and now he's playing a position with a high offensive bar. That made him expendable.

    Industry observers note that lewis, 27, was under team control through 2028 and that extra year was an crucial consideration for the club. His salary would have been in the $5 million range next season through arbitration, which is pricey but not exorbitant. Now, Lewis will receive a fresh start with the Dodgers, where he can be one of the guys, not the former No. 1 overall pick and expected face of the franchise.

    The Twins presumably did not want to give up on a player with as much talent as Lewis. At the same time, they kept trying, and it never worked.

    The Twins got a head start on their offseason bullpen shopping when they acquired Jeff Hoffman at the trade deadline. He has one more year remaining on the contract and will be in the team's late-inning mix in 2027.

    Here is manager Derek Shelton's bullpen unit at the moment:.

    Morris is not yet a household name, but he has a great arm and was dominant at times in 2026. The Twins have themselves a nice little late-inning trio in Gómez, Hoffman, and Morris. A spare starter like Matthews or Prielipp could wind up in the bullpen as well. Given the quality of their stuff, they have a chance to make a real impact as relievers.

    Recent findings suggest that clearly though, the middle relief could use some help, and the Twins wouldn't need to spend massive dollars to improve it. A second-tier free agent like, say, Andrew Kittredge would be a solid pickup. It's worth giving the Miami Marlins a call to see what it would take to get Anthony Bender and/or Michael Petersen. Point is, the bullpen can be improved, for sure.

    In a recent development, the Twins have way more outfielders than outfield spots and that is in no way a bad thing. First and foremost, it allows them to use Byron Buxton as the full-time DH, which could help keep him on the field. Secondly, there's no such thing as too many good players. Depth is vital and the Twins certainly have plenty of it in the outfield.

    Industry observers note that more outfielders than outfield spots is not a problem. It's just something the Twins have to figure out. Even if we assume Buxton will DH and is not part of the outfield mix, here are the outfielders Minnesota must sort through:.

    According to recent reports, rodriguez is one of the game's 50 or so best prospects and he is out of minor league options, meaning he must go through waivers to go to Triple-A. Obviously, the Twins won't waive him. Non-tendering Larnach allows the Twins to play Rodriguez alongside Jenkins and Keaschall in the outfield, keep Kreidler and Martin on the bench, and keep the others in Triple-A.

    #164907. Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect

    Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No.
    • Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline.
    • The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the New York Post. Neither team has confirmed the trade.

    Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.

    The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the significant leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.

    It has been revealed that miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control challenges since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.

    In a recent development, espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.

    Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.

    At worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the new Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.

    Espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant.

    It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.

    Industry observers note that it's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.

    Sources indicate that giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it.

    The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

    Breaking: MLB rumors: Yankees moves heating up, plus latest on Tarik Skubal, Mets, Padres, Red Sox, more

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1104 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • The buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free-agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Friday's supply just below.

    The buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio. If the deal is worth at least $390 million, it would set new records for total guarantee and average annual value given to a pitcher. Here are the current pitcher contract records:.

    Sources indicate that 1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    Sources indicate that 2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    In a recent development, 3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Given the player and the deep-pocketed teams involved in the bidding (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), Skubal is well-positioned to shatter Yamamoto's record. He could beat Scherzer's and Verlander's record as well. The expected lockout will begin after the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Skubal is likely to sign before then.

    The Diamondbacks are set to acquire righty Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later, reports the Arizona Republic. Boston had four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Oviedo, Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck) and always seemed likely to trade one to ease the logjam.

    Acquired from the Pirates last offseason, Oviedo made just one ineffective appearance around elbow trouble in 2026. He returned from Tommy John surgery in 2025 and looked excellent, and Arizona will hope Oviedo rediscovers that magic as he gets further away from his injuries. Dotson is not a top prospect. It's a low-cost flier for the D-backs.

    Industry observers note that the Tigers have signed right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year extension worth $46.5 million, reports ESPN. There is a club option for a seventh year and escalators can push the total guarantee to $80 million. Melton still had five years of team control. The new extension buys out his five team control years and one free agent year with an option for another free agent year.

    Melton, 26 next month, missed the start of the season with elbow inflammation and finished the season on the injured list with more elbow woes. Between injuries, he made 20 starts with a sub-3.00 ERA with strong under-the-hood numbers. The Tigers know him better than anyone and are obviously comfortable with Melton's medicals to lock him up long-term.

    According to recent reports, the New York Yankees have agreed to a two-year contract with veteran right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga, ESPN reports. The deal also includes a club option for 2029 and is worth roughly $18 million, according to MLB.com.

    Loáisiga, 32, is coming off that strong season above for the Arizona Diamondbacks, and for his career boasts an ERA+ of 128 across parts of nine MLB seasons. He's worked in relief for almost all of that span, and eight of those nine seasons came with the Yankees.

    According to recent reports, upcoming York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman was recently asked if he'd be willing to play Spencer Jones in center field. In response, he told media, including SNY, this:.

    Recent findings suggest that "I would be comfortable with that. At the same time Jasson Domínguez is pounding the ball in winter ball. The entire industry is noticing that based on the phone calls I'm getting.".

    The 23-year-old Domínguez still has big-time power potential, and defensively he's best suited to center field. For his career in the Bronx, he has an OPS+ of 93, but his 751 plate appearances have been doled out erratically across four seasons. As things stand now, he'll once again be subject to a playing-time crunch. Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger are installed at the outfield corners, and Giancarlo Stanton, if healthy, should get much of the playing time at DH. That leaves center field for Jones or Domínguez. Other teams no doubt see that bottleneck and are seeing if Cashman and the Yankees are willing to relieve it through trade.

    Lefty ace and two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal remains far and away the top talent on the free-agent market. While the New York Mets and incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers seem like the favorites to secure his services, the San Diego Padres also have significant interest in him. That interest took the next step on Thursday with an in-person meeting, The Athletic reports. The Padres are the fourth team to meet with Skubal, who turned 30 on Friday. Previously, the Dodgers, Mets, and Toronto Blue Jays met with him.

    Industry observers note that the Padres have a pronounced need in the rotation, especially if free-agent right-hander Michael King signs elsewhere. Last winter, they also lost Dylan Cease to the Blue Jays via free agency.

    Industry observers note that the Padres and left-handed platoon hitter Gavin Sheets have agreed to a three-year, $11 million contract extension that includes two opt-outs, FanSided reports. Sheets, who'll turn 31 in April, had been slated for free agency after the upcoming season. Instead, he and the Padres will now be potentially committed through the 2029 season, depending on whether Sheets exercises any of his opt-outs. While he's not much of a hitter for average, he does draw walks and hit for power. In two seasons with San Diego, he's tallied 36 home runs and 44 doubles in 855 at-bats while seeing DH, first base, and the outfield corners.

    The New York Mets have agreed to a three-year, $12 million deal with right-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernández, reports José F. Rivera.

    Recent findings suggest that hernández, who turns 30 in December, hasn't pitched in MLB since 2022 and instead has revived his career with four strong seasons in Japan. Over that span for Softbank of the NPB, he's put up an ERA of 2.46 in 131 ⅔ innings with 168 strikeouts and 42 unintentional walks. Prior to rebuilding himself in Japan, Hernández had a 5.06 ERA and a 1.82 K/BB ratio over parts of four seasons with the Boston Red Sox.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball.
    • In a recent development, most such decisions are easy and obvious.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball. That crucial date on the offseason calendar is when clubs must make, or "tender," contract offers for the upcoming season to all their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players on the 40-player roster. That's every player who isn't a free agent or isn't presently signed to a multi-year contract. Players who are tendered a contract by that deadline remain with their current organizations. Players who aren't offered a contract become free agents.

    In a recent development, most such decisions are easy and obvious. Others, however, present difficult calls for the organization because of roster crunches, crowded depth charts, or, more commonly, reluctance to retain a player as his salary rises through the arbitration process. While a number of non-tendered players are likely on their way out of the league, a select few others qualify as at least interesting to other teams and, on occasion, a few will even be coveted to varying degrees.

    All that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire. Let's get to it ….

    According to recent reports, the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year, Gil has been injured and ineffective the last two seasons. He missed time with a shoulder matter this past season and also spent time in Triple-A. The Yankees moved him to the bullpen late in the season to see whether he could contribute that way, though Gil was unable to make a strong impression in that role. Now 28, Gil still has another three seasons of team control remaining. Whichever team signs him will be able to keep him through 2029, and that extra control, plus his Rookie of the Year pedigree, will no doubt land Gil with a fresh team before Opening Day.

    According to recent reports, as a 23-year-old in 2023, the infielder and former first-rounder hit 27 home runs in 119 games and looked like a future cornerstone for the Cardinals. Gorman, however, has gotten steadily worse since then thanks largely to his persistent strikeout concerns. Last season, he wound up back at Triple-A for an extended stretch and didn't fare any better upon being recalled. Long-term, the Cardinals will likely look to hand the third base position to rising power prospect Jesús Báez, who was recently added to the 40-player roster. Gorman can be a plus at third and probably still get by at second, and no doubt some team will take a chance on his power.

    On the downside, Larnach is a defensive minus at the corner outfield spots and probably needs to be a DH, and he's also a platoon bat. On the upside, he's been a steady producer from the left side of the plate. This past season, he put up a .352 OBP and an OPS+ of 120 for Minnesota. For his career, he has an OPS+ of 106 across parts of six MLB seasons. He out-hit his underlying indicators by a bit in 2026, but Larnach is still going to be an appealing part-time bat for some teams.

    Recent findings suggest that the Twins cut bait on a right-hander who's made 139 career starts for them since his 2021 major-league debut. Ober boasts a career OPS+ of 102, but that figure has slid over the last two seasons. What's also slid is Ober's fastball velocity, which may be why he's on this list. In his rookie season, he averaged a fringy 92.4 mph with his four-seamer, but last season that figure was down all the way to 88 mph. That put him in the very bottom percentile among MLB hurlers. The 31-year-old Ober still should draw some interest as a depth piece.

    A platoon extraordinaire, Raley has always hit for power against righties, including 15 home runs in only 290 plate appearances against them in 2026. He's sneaky fast and a very good athlete for his size (6-foot-3 and 235 lbs.), good enough to handle the corner outfield spots competently. Raley also has first base experience and can patrol center field in a pinch. The Mariners cut him loose even though he will remain under team control through 2028. Raley's power against righties and an extra year of control could make him a solid bench option moving forward.
